title: AgentClinic: a multimodal agent benchmark to evaluate AI in simulated clinical environments
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the impact of implicit 'religion bias' on the performance of LLMs in simulated clinical environments. This was measured by introducing a bias prompt related to religion to either the 'doctor agent' or the 'patient agent' and then assessing the resulting diagnostic accuracy and the patient agent's perception of the doctor (in terms of confidence, compliance, and willingness to consult again).
findings: When implicit religion bias was introduced, it had a profound negative effect on all three categories of patient perception ratings (confidence, compliance, and consultation). For patient confidence, the effect of religion bias was significant, following behind gender bias. For patient compliance and consultation ratings, religion bias also ranked among the more impactful biases. The diagnostic accuracy of Mixtral-8x7B was more negatively affected by religion bias than GPT-4, which showed more resilience.
